title: Cross your fingers, touch your nose: two noses
pause_note: v5, Your Brain Is Tricking You, hook=try len=short look=flat. DO hook at 0 s: crossed fingers land on the nose tip with a pink touch ripple at 0.5 s (Aristotle illusion; one nose in frame 0, the "two" is first shown at the 8.4 s reveal); 1.4 s hold = clean touch moment; wrong guess (numb / confused fingers) killed at ~5 s; reveal at ~8 s: the brain still uses the uncrossed finger map, the nose splits in two on the stage; outer sides explained inside the zoomed fingertips; Aristotle 2,300+ years ago; one-word question ("Two?"); loop to frame one. No mascot.

beats: Cross two fingers and rub the tip of your nose.
Feels like two? It's not your fingers.
Your brain still thinks they're uncrossed.
Then these outer sides could only touch two different things. So it feels two noses.
Aristotle wrote about this trick over two thousand years ago.
